full_judgment:
A.M. Mahmudur Rahman, J:— This Rule is against an order dated March 24, 1986 of the Upazila Munsif, Sadar, Brahmanbaria allowing Misc. Case No. 38A of 1984, filed under Section 151 C.P.C. and setting aside the order of dismissal dated 28.1.85 passed in the said Miscellaneous Case. 

 2. The petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 151 of 1983 in the court of Munsif, Second Court, Brahmanbaria for declaration that certain property is not vested property and the property belonged to them on the basis of purchase from original owner. In the said suit the defendant appeared on 19.5.84 and prayed for time to file written statement. The learned Munsif allowed the prayer and fixed 21.6.84 for that purpose, but on that date the defendant did not take any step and accordingly, 25.6.84 was fixed for exparte disposal of the suit. On 25.6.84, the defendant did not take any steps and the suit was decreed ex-parte. Thereafter, on 26.7.84, the defendant filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure of setting aside the ex-parte decree on the ground that the learned Advocate did not enter the date for filing written statement in his diary. The miscellaneous case was contested by the petitioner by filing written objection on 10.12.84. Thereafter, the case was fixed for hearing on 28.1.85, but the defendant did not again take any step and the Miscellaneous-case was dismissed for default. Later on, the defendant opposite-party, on March 3, 1986, filed an application under section 151 C.P.C for setting aside the order of dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case passed on 28.1.85. The learned Munsif, upon such application, by an ex-parte order dated 24.3.86, set aside the order of dismissal of the miscellaneous case and restored the same to its original filed and number. 

 3. Mr. Abdus Sattar, the learned Advocated appearing in support of the Rule, submits that the order of dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case filed under Order 9 Rule 1(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. As the code provided for an appeal from such order of dismissal of the Miscellaneous case, the order impugned before me passed by invoking jurisdiction under section 151 C.P.C. we absolutely illegal and is liable to be struck down. The impugned order is as follows:- 

 that the dismissal order dated 28.1.85 be set aside and the original Misc. Case be restored to its file and number. To 17.4.86 for steps." 

 4. Where a Code provides an alternative remedy the provision of section 151 C.P.C. is not available. In this case the order of dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case being appealable order, the court below committed an error of law in its decision. Not only that, from the above quoted order, it is difficult to understand the reason for which the application was allowed and the impugned order not being a speaking order is also liable to be struck down on that score alone. 

 5. For the reasons stated above. I set aside the impugned order passed by the learned Munsif and dismiss the Miscellaneous case No. 28A of 1984, pending in this court. The connected stay order is vacated.
